_LANG_RULE: Write in {name}, this run's language. If the player writes in another language, understand it, but keep narration, spoken lines and options in {name}.
_SOUL_LANG: Speak in {name}, even if the player uses another language.

SPEC.head:
## Output format
Follow this format exactly. Write nothing outside the blocks.
SPEC.lines: lines: the messages shown on screen, in order. A character's spoken line must be wrapped in quotation marks (starts with ", ends with "). A message without quotation marks is narration. Never put speech and narration in the same message. This feeds an ADV text panel: one sentence per line.
SPEC.ops: ops: this turn's state changes, one per line; if nothing changed write a single line: none. Allowed lines:
SPEC.options: options: 2–4 things the player might say or do next. Short (under 12 words), pointing in different directions (friendly / confrontational / change the subject …). One option per line.Of them: when someone here can be talked to, make one '@Name what you say to them, ask them or ask them to do' (the name as listed among those present); when one of the player's skills fits, make one '/Skill target or aim' (the skill name exactly as on the player's sheet, no number); when neither fits, do not force it. Each choice is plain words, with no brackets around it.
SPEC.inline: An action may also be written inline in lines, equivalent to an ops line: [~move player inn]You push the inn door open., or [~flag paid]. A request in square brackets stops the lines at that line; the engine answers and you continue. The engine speaks back to you in angle brackets: <event>/<end> are things that happened, <say> a character's line, <roll 1d6>4</roll> a request's answer, <refused> why something was refused.
SPEC.example:
<cot>Player takes a room at the inn; pays 8.</cot>
<lines>
You push open the inn door; the hearth's warmth touches your face.
"One room."
The innkeeper looks up from the counter and takes you in.
"Eight coins a night, paid up front."
</lines>
<ops>
move player inn
player.gold -8
</ops>
<options>
"Pay for one night"
Ask the innkeeper about strangers in town
"Too expensive"
Turn around and leave
</options>

_VAR_LINE: {var} -3          variable: name + number; a leading + / − adds, no sign sets

HEAD.reports: # Character replies (already happened this turn; inside <say name>…</say> only the words in quotation marks are quoted verbatim as one line, first-person text outside them is her action — write it in third person; to= is where she heads, write the move)
HEAD.prefix: # Already written (shown to the player, final; continue from its last line, never rewrite or repeat a line)
HEAD.mentions: # Named but not present (the player mentioned them; this is where they are)
HEAD.cont: # Continue: output only the continuing <lines>, the whole turn's <ops> (including what already happened) and <options>
HEAD.refused: # Last proposal refused (fix only these, keep the rest)
HEAD.tools: # Tool results (your requests, already run by the engine; continue from that line, use these results, do not re-roll or repeat the request)

_CONTEXT_DOC:
# This world's context language (generated by the engine; do not hand-edit — regenerate after changing manifest.json → prompt)

## What the engine shows the model each turn (the pack)
In order: time · town / here / exits · place ids of this town · present characters and NPCs · player · personas · characters elsewhere · notes / rumors / lore · registered classes · engine messages · variables and their rules · recent narration.
Then the user block: tool results · character replies · relevant entries · the player now · (on refusal) the last proposal.

## What the model writes (output format)
{blocks}

## The context language: the bracket says whether the turn waits
- `[tag args]` a sync request: lines stop at that line; the engine answers and the model continues (`[dice 1d20+2 vs 12]why[/dice]`, `[referee what the player attempts]`, `[ask <name>]`, `[combat bandit×3]hand-off[/combat]`)
- `[~tag args]` an async action: not awaited, the engine does it and the model keeps writing (`[~move player inn]`, `[~flag paid]`, `[~player.gold -3]`, `[~map]`); same as one ops line
- The engine's registry decides which ops wait (each op declares `wait`); a wrong bracket is executed by the registry and logged in the trace
- The old form `<move player inn>` is still read, as `[~move player inn]`
The engine speaks back in angle brackets: `<event id>what happened</event>` · `<end id>epilogue hint</end>` · `<say name attitude=…>line</say>` · `<roll 1d6>4</roll>` · `<refused op field>why; allowed: …</refused>`.

## Ops registered in this world (generated from the actions table)
{ops}

## Entries (manifest.json → "prompt" → "entries"; play-time changes in game/meta/prompt.json)
- `"when": "always"` goes into the system prompt; `"post"` goes last; conditional ones (`{{"keyword": …}}` · `{{"at": …}}` · `{{"var": …, ">=": n}}` · `{{"flag": …}}`) are injected next to the player's line when they hold.
- `rules` / `voice` / `blocks` / `ops_docs` live here too. Three layers: the template's pack.json < manifest.json < game/meta/prompt.json.

_STYLE_SAY.divider: Start each block with its own line === name === (e.g. === lines ===); no closing marker — the next block's line ends the previous one.
_STYLE_SAY.fence: Open each block with its own line ```name (e.g. ```lines) and close it with a line ```.

_ASYNC_SAY.angle: Square brackets [ ] are requests you wait for (stop at that line); angle brackets < > are actions not waited for (the engine does them, you keep writing).
_ASYNC_SAY.tilde: Square brackets [ ] are requests you wait for (stop at that line); square brackets opening with ~ [~ ] are actions not waited for (the engine does them, you keep writing), e.g. [~move player inn], [~map].

_CROSS_LANG: This world's material is written in {src}; it is only source material. Write every line of prose, dialogue and options in {name} — not one sentence in {src}. Proper names may keep their original form.
